mainTopic: יוכבד completes the seventy, יוסף's descendants defeat עשו's, and what a בכור takes a double share of (priestly gifts, sacrificial animals, natural growth of the estate).
overview: This amud begins by finishing a challenge to the count of seventy people who went down to מצרים. The answer is that יוכבד is the seventieth: she was conceived on the way and born in מצרים. Then רבי חלבו asks why יעקב wanted to leave לבן only after יוסף was born. The answer is that only יוסף's descendants can defeat עשו's descendants. Two challenges follow, from דוד and from men of שמעון who struck עמלק. Each is answered by showing that leaders from מנשה, a son of יוסף, were involved. The גמרא then turns to a ברייתא about the בכור's double share: priestly gifts, sacrificial animals, and growth of the estate after the father's death. It explains each item in turn. On the last item, it begins explaining why the ברייתא lists both a rented cow and a grazing cow, and that explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The את before בנימין would break the count of seventy
steps.stepSummary: The questioner points to the word את before בנימין. If את adds an extra person here as well, the count of seventy no longer works.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And את בנימין his brother, his mother's son"?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began just before this. The questioner points to the word את before בנימין's name, as if it also adds an extra person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every את adds a hidden extra person, this verse adds one more to יעקב's family. That would ruin the exact total of seventy people who went down to מצרים.

keyTerms.meaning: A small Hebrew word that marks the object; sometimes read as including something extra
His mother's son (a full brother, from the same mother)

phrases.english: "And et Binyamin his brother, his mother's son"?!
phrases.notes: This finishes the challenge from just before: if את adds someone here, the count of seventy is off. בראשית 43:29.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of seventy who went down to מצרים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If את adds a person here too, there is one person too many

steps.title: יוכבד is the seventieth person
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא defends his treasured teaching. The seventieth person is יוכבד, who was conceived on the way and born inside מצרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: I had a fine pearl in my hand, and you want to make me lose it! This is what רבי חמא בר חנינא said: the seventieth person is יוכבד. She was conceived on the journey and born inside the walls of מצרים. The פסוק says she was born to לוי "in מצרים," which means her birth was in מצרים but her conception was not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר אבא answers that the count of seventy is already complete with יוכבד, so you cannot add more people. He calls this teaching a precious pearl he refuses to give up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The named list comes to sixty-nine, and יוכבד makes seventy. The proof comes from the words "born in מצרים." They show that only her birth happened there, so her mother was already pregnant on the way down. Because the seventy are already accounted for, there is no room for an extra twin from את בנימין.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine pearl (here, a precious teaching)
Daughter of לוי, mother of משה

steps.whatToRemember: The seventy who went down to מצרים are completed by יוכבד, who was conceived on the way and born in מצרים.

phrases.english: He said: A fine pearl was in my hand,
phrases.notes: The one speaking is רבי חייא בר אבא, answering the challenge.

phrases.english: and you want to make me lose it;

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: This is what Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said:
This is Yocheved,
phrases.notes: He means: the missing seventieth person is יוכבד.

phrases.english: whose conception was on the way,
and whose birth was between the walls;
as it is said:
"whom she bore to Levi in Egypt":
her birth was in Egypt,
but her conception was not in Egypt.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the seventieth person, so the count is already complete
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought את בנימין could add another person
steps.terutzMaskana: The seventy are already complete with יוכבד, so no extra person can be added

steps.title: Why did יעקב want to leave only after יוסף was born?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו asks רבי שמואל בר נחמני what was special about יוסף's birth that made יעקב decide to go home.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חלבו asked רבי שמואל בר נחמני: It is written, "And it was, when רחל gave birth to יוסף," that יעקב asked לבן to let him go home. What was different once יוסף was born?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins here. רבי חלבו asks why the פסוק links יעקב's wish to leave לבן with the moment יוסף was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק places יעקב's request right after יוסף's birth. That suggests יוסף's birth changed something, and the question is what it changed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chelbo asked
of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani:
It is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיְהִי כַּאֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה רָחֵל אֶת יוֹסֵף וְגוֹ׳״ –
phrases.english: "And it was, when Rachel gave birth to Yosef, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:25. The rest of the פסוק has יעקב asking לבן to send him home.

phrases.english: What is different when Yosef was born?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חֶלְבּוֹ מֵרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why יוסף's birth was the trigger for יעקב to leave לבן

steps.title: Only יוסף's descendants defeat עשו's
steps.stepSummary: יעקב saw that עשו's descendants would be handed over only to יוסף's descendants. Once יוסף was born, he felt safe going back.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יעקב our father saw that עשו's descendants are handed over only into the hands of יוסף's descendants, as it says: "The house of יעקב shall be fire, the house of יוסף a flame, and the house of עשו straw."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains that יוסף is the one whose family can overpower עשו. That is why יעקב felt ready to return home once יוסף was born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from עובדיה, where the house of יוסף is the flame that burns the straw of עשו. The answer also sets up a firm rule: only יוסף's descendants defeat עשו's. The next steps will test that rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule that the next two challenges will test.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Yaakov our father saw
that the descendants of Esav are not handed over
except into the hand of the descendants of Yosef,
as it is said:
"And the house of Yaakov shall be fire,
and the house of Yosef a flame,
and the house of Esav straw, etc."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only יוסף's descendants defeat עשו's descendants, so יעקב could safely return once יוסף was born

steps.title: But דוד defeated עמלק
steps.stepSummary: רבי חלבו objects: דוד, who came from יהודה, struck עמלק, who come from עשו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected to him: "And דוד struck them from twilight until the evening of the next day"!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חלבו challenges the rule with a פסוק that shows דוד defeating עמלק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עמלק comes from עשו, and דוד was from שבט יהודה, not from יוסף. So it seems someone other than יוסף's descendants did defeat עשו's descendants.

phrases.english: He objected to him:
"And David struck them from twilight
phrases.notes: "Them" is עמלק, who come from עשו. דוד is from יהודה, not יוסף.

phrases.english: until the evening of the next day"!

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only יוסף's descendants defeat עשו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דוד from יהודה defeated עמלק, who come from עשו

steps.title: דוד's army was led by men of מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני answers from דברי הימים: leaders from מנשה, a son of יוסף, joined דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Whoever taught you נביאים did not teach you כתובים! For it is written: "When he went to צקלג, men from מנשה joined him: עדנה, יוזבד, ידיעאל, מיכאל, יוזבד, אליהוא, and צלתי, heads of the thousands of מנשה."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני answers with a פסוק from כתובים showing that captains from מנשה fought on דוד's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנשה is a son of יוסף. So דוד's victory over עמלק still came through יוסף's descendants, and the rule holds. The playful line means: if you had learned כתובים too, you would know this.

keyTerms.meaning: צקלג, the town where דוד stayed

phrases.english: He said to him:
The one who taught you Prophets
did not teach you Writings;
as it is written:
"When he went to Tziklag,
there fell to him from Menashe
phrases.notes: "Fell to him" means they joined his side.

phrases.english: Adnah, and Yozavad, and Yediael,
and Michael, and Yozavad, and Elihu, and Tziltai,
heads of the thousands of Menashe."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דְּאַקְרְיָךְ נְבִיאֵי לָא אַקְרְיָךְ כְּתוּבֵי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows from another פסוק that the fighters really came from יוסף's line
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד alone, from יהודה, defeated עמלק
steps.terutzMaskana: Men of מנשה led the fight, so יוסף's descendants were involved

steps.title: But men of שמעון struck עמלק
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects: men from שבט שמעון went to הר שעיר and struck the last of עמלק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: "And some of them, from the sons of שמעון, five hundred men, went to הר שעיר, led by פלטיה, נעריה, רפיה, and עזיאל, the sons of ישעי. They struck the remnant of עמלק that had escaped and settled there to this day"!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a second challenge to the rule. Here the fighters against עמלק seem to come from שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the פסוק names שמעון, not יהודה. So it again looks like non-יוסף tribes defeated עשו's descendants.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Seir, the land of עשו

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects:
"And of them, from the sons of Shimon,
went to Mount Seir
five hundred men,
and Pelatyah, and Nearyah, and Refayah, and Uziel,
the sons of Yishi, at their head,
and they struck the remnant of Amalek that had escaped,
and they settled there until this day"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the rule from step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only יוסף's descendants defeat עשו

steps.title: ישעי came from מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא answers that the leaders' father, ישעי, was from מנשה, so the leaders were from יוסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא said: ישעי came from the sons of מנשה, as it is written: "And the sons of מנשה: חפר and ישעי."
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא answers רב יוסף: the leaders of the attack were sons of ישעי, and ישעי was from מנשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The soldiers were from שמעון, but their leaders came from מנשה, a son of יוסף. So once again the victory over עשו came through יוסף's line, and the rule stands.
steps.whatToRemember: Every case where עשו's descendants are defeated turns out to involve leaders from יוסף, through מנשה. This supports why יעקב felt safe once יוסף was born.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila said:
Yishi came from the sons of Menashe,
as it is written:
"And the sons of Menashe: Chefer and Yishi."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שֵׁילָא: יִשְׁעִי מִבְּנֵי מְנַשֶּׁה אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Traces the leaders' family back to מנשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The victory came from שבט שמעון alone
steps.terutzMaskana: The leaders were sons of ישעי from מנשה, so יוסף's descendants led the fight

steps.title: A ברייתא lists what the בכור takes a double share of
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the בכור takes a double portion of the priestly gifts, of sacrificial animals, and of growth in the property after the father's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The בכור takes a double portion of the foreleg, the jaw, and the maw. He also takes a double portion of sacrificial animals, and of the growth in the property after their father died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא that lists three kinds of property where the בכור gets a double share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg, jaw, and maw are the gifts every כהן receives from slaughtered animals, so this part is about a בכור whose father was a כהן. The list also includes growth in the estate after the father's death, which seems surprising, since that growth was never in the father's hands. The next lines of the ברייתא and the גמרא will explain both of these items.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who inherits a double portion
Foreleg, jaw, and maw: gifts given to a כהן from slaughtered animals
Increase in value or growth of property

steps.confusionAlert: The double share of the foreleg, jaw, and maw only applies when the father was a כהן, since only a כהן receives those gifts.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The firstborn takes a double portion
of the foreleg, and of the jaw, and of the maw,
phrases.notes: These are the gifts a כהן gets from every slaughtered animal (דברים 18:3).

phrases.english: and of sacrificial animals,
and of the growth by which the property increased
after their father's death.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the בכור's inheritance, separate from the discussion of יעקב and יוסף in steps 3-8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בכור takes a double portion of the priestly gifts, of sacrificial animals, and of growth in the estate after the father's death.

steps.title: Which kind of growth counts for the double share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains that natural growth, such as rent or a cow giving birth, counts for the double share. Growth the heirs produce, like building houses or planting vineyards, does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? Suppose their father left them a cow that was leased or rented out to others, or that was grazing in the meadow, and it gave birth. Then the בכור takes a double portion. But if the heirs built houses or planted vineyards, the בכור does not take a double portion.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains what it meant by 'growth after the father's death.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rent from a cow, or a calf that is born, grows out of the father's own property without the heirs doing anything, so it counts as part of his estate. Houses and vineyards come from the heirs' own work and investment, so the בכור gets no extra share of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Leased (paid in produce) or rented (paid in money)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the boundary for the בכור's double share. Growth that comes on its own from the father's property counts. Growth the heirs create through their own effort does not.

phrases.english: How so?
Their father left them a cow
that was leased or rented out in the hands of others,
or that was grazing in the meadow;
and it gave birth: the firstborn takes a double portion.
But if they built houses and planted vineyards,
the firstborn does not take a double portion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא explains the last item on its list in step 9: growth after the father's death.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Natural growth of the father's property (rent, offspring) is shared double. Improvements the heirs make (houses, vineyards) are not.

steps.title: How can the בכור get a double share of the priestly gifts?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. If the gifts already reached the father, the ruling is obvious. If they did not, they are only 'due' property, and a בכור does not take double of that.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the foreleg, jaw, and maw: what is the case? If they had already come into the father's hands, it is obvious that the בכור takes double. And if they had not come into the father's hands, they are only property that was due to him, and the בכור does not take double of property that was due the way he does of property the father held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first item in the ברייתא. Both ways of picturing the case seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father already received the gifts, they are simply his property, and the ברייתא would have no reason to say it. If he never received them, they fall under the rule that a בכור gets no double share of property that was only due to the father. So the ruling seems either pointless or wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (asks for the exact situation)
Property that was due to the father but not yet in his hands

phrases.english: This foreleg, and jaw, and maw:
what is the case?
If they came into their father's hands,
it is obvious!
And if they did not come into their father's hands,
it is only property that was due,
and the firstborn does not take of what was due as he does of what was held!
phrases.notes: The double share only covers what the father actually owned when he died, not what was still coming to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי הַזְּרוֹעַ וְהַלְּחָיַיִם וְהַקֵּיבָה – הֵיכִי דָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the first item of the ברייתא in step 9 and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 9 that the בכור takes a double share of the foreleg, jaw, and maw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both ways of reading the case fail. Either the ruling is obvious, or it goes against the rule that a בכור gets no double share of רָאוּי.

steps.title: Gifts not yet separated count as already separated
steps.stepSummary: The case is a כהן with regular givers whose animal was slaughtered in his lifetime. The ברייתא holds that unseparated gifts count as separated, so they already belonged to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here we are dealing with people who regularly give their gifts to a particular כהן, and the animal was slaughtered while the father was alive. The author of the ברייתא holds that priestly gifts not yet separated are treated as if they were already separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by describing a special case where the gifts already count as the father's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because these givers always give to this one כהן, the gifts were set aside for him. Once the animal was slaughtered in his lifetime, the gifts count as if already separated and in his hands, even before they were physically handed over. That makes them מוּחְזָק and not רָאוּי, so the בכור takes double. The ruling is also not obvious, because it depends on this view about unseparated gifts.

keyTerms.meaning: People who regularly give their priestly gifts to one particular כהן
He holds (introduces the view behind a ruling)

steps.whatToRemember: The בכור of a כהן takes double of priestly gifts only in this special case: the givers were regular, the animal was slaughtered in the father's lifetime, and we hold that unseparated gifts count as separated. Then the gifts are the father's held property (מוּחְזָק), not merely due (רָאוּי).

phrases.english: Here we are dealing with acquaintances of the priesthood,
phrases.notes: These are people who always give their gifts to the same כהן.

phrases.english: and the animal was slaughtered during their father's lifetime;
and he holds:
gifts that were not separated
are considered as if they were separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 11 by finding a case that is neither obvious nor רָאוּי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) together with a legal view about unseparated gifts.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The priestly gifts are either already received, so the ruling is obvious, or merely due, so the בכור gets no double share.
steps.terutzMaskana: For regular givers, once the animal is slaughtered in the father's lifetime, the gifts count as already separated and held by him, so the בכור takes double.

steps.title: Sacrificial animals don't belong to the father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: how can the בכור take double of sacrificial animals, if those animals no longer belong to the father?
steps.simpleTranslation: Sacrificial animals? They are not his!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks another item in the ברייתא's list: sacrificial animals (מוקדשין). Once something is consecrated, it seems to belong to Heaven, not to the father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור only takes double of property the father actually owned. If consecrated animals belong to Heaven, there is nothing of the father's for the בכור to inherit, so the ברייתא seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not his; they are not his property

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals – they are not his!
phrases.notes: This goes back to the ברייתא from step 9, which listed sacrificial animals among the things the בכור takes double of.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After resolving the priestly gifts in step 12, the גמרא moves on to the next item in the ברייתא: sacrificial animals.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the בכור takes double of sacrificial animals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consecrated animals belong to Heaven, so they are not the father's property, and a בכור only doubles the father's property.

steps.title: Lighter offerings count as the owner's property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is talking about קדשים קלים and follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that such offerings are the owner's property. He learns this from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about offerings of lesser holiness, and it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says they are the owner's property. As a ברייתא teaches: 'And commits a trespass against ה׳' comes to include offerings of lesser holiness, which are the owner's property. These are the words of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means only קדשים קלים, like a שלמים, and follows רבי יוסי הגלילי. In his view these animals still count as the owner's money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי reads the פסוק about someone who denies holding his friend's property ('and commits a trespass against ה׳') as including קדשים קלים. That shows the Torah treats them as the owner's own property. Since they were the father's, the בכור can take double of them.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, such as a שלמים
To include, meaning the פסוק adds another case

phrases.english: With offerings of lesser sanctity,
and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili –
who says: it is the owner's property.
As it is taught: "And commits a trespass against the Lord" –

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבּוֹת קֳדָשִׁים קַלִּים, שֶׁהֵן מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים;
phrases.english: to include offerings of lesser sanctity, which are the owner's property;
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by narrowing the case and tying it to one תנא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (קדשים קלים) and assigning it to a specific opinion (רבי יוסי הגלילי)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All sacrificial animals belong to Heaven, so the father owned none of them.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, קדשים קלים are the owner's property, so the בכור takes double of them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the ברייתא's list depends on a specific view about who owns קדשים קלים.

steps.title: The ברייתא's case of a rented or grazing cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's case: a cow the father left was rented out or grazing in a meadow and gave birth. The בכור takes double.
steps.simpleTranslation: If their father left them a cow that was leased or rented out to others, or that was grazing in the meadow, and it gave birth, the בכור takes a double portion of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes this line of the ברייתא again because it is about to ask a question on it. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two cases of natural growth: a cow out on rent, and a cow grazing in the meadow. Both produce growth after the father's death, and the בכור takes double in both. The גמרא will now ask why both cases are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Leased out for a fixed payment

phrases.english: If their father left them a cow
leased or rented in the possession of others,
or if it was grazing in the meadow;

phrases.aramaic: וְיָלְדָה – בְּכוֹר נוֹטֵל בָּהּ פִּי שְׁנַיִם.
phrases.english: and it gave birth – the firstborn takes a double portion of it.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the opening of the question in step 16)
steps.triggerLanguage: הִנִּיחַ לָהֶן אֲבִיהֶן פָּרָה מוּחְכֶּרֶת וּמוּשְׂכֶּרֶת בְּיַד אֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with sacrificial animals, the גמרא turns to the ברייתא's case of natural growth (first summarized in step 10) in order to question it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A cow out on rent or grazing that gives birth after the father's death counts as growth that the בכור takes double of.

steps.title: Why mention the grazing cow at all?
steps.stepSummary: If the בכור takes double even of a rented cow that isn't in the owners' hands, it is obvious that he takes double of a cow grazing in the meadow, which is still in their hands. So why state the grazing case?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, if a leased or rented cow, which is not in its owners' possession, you say he takes double, is it even necessary to say so for a cow grazing in the meadow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא bothers to mention the grazing cow. The rented case is the harder one, so the grazing case seems obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rented cow is in someone else's hands, so you might think it is less fully the heirs' property. Even so, the בכור takes double. A grazing cow is fully in the owners' hands, so it should go without saying, and the ברייתא seems to have an extra case.

keyTerms.meaning: Now if [the harder case is true], is [the easier case] even necessary to say?

phrases.english: Now, a leased or rented cow –
which is not standing in the possession of its owners,
you say he takes [double];
one grazing in the meadow, is it necessary [to say]?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's mention of the grazing cow
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is a 'how much more so' argument: if the harder case (rented out) gets double, the easier case (grazing at home) obviously does, so stating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The rented cow is like the grazing cow
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentions the grazing cow to teach that the rented cow is just like it: the growth comes by itself and the brothers spend nothing on feeding it. The answer continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches us: that a leased or rented cow is like one grazing in the meadow. Just as with a grazing cow the growth comes by itself and the brothers don't lose money on its food...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the grazing case is not extra. It is there to show what the rented case is like. The sentence is not finished here; it continues in the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the two cases side by side teaches what they have in common. In both, the growth happens naturally and the heirs pay nothing for feeding. That shared feature is why the בכור takes double, and it fits the rule from step 10 that only natural growth counts.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison works in the opposite direction from what you might expect. The grazing case is not a new law; it explains the condition under which the rented case gets double.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches us –
that a leased or rented cow is similar to one grazing in the meadow;
just as one grazing in the meadow –
the enhancement comes by itself,
and they do not lose [money] on its food;
phrases.notes: 'They' are the brothers. The thought keeps going on the next part of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 by explaining why the ברייתא needed the grazing case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison (דומיא): the extra case defines the condition for the main case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The grazing case is obvious and seems to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The grazing case teaches that the rented cow gets double only because its growth, like the grazing cow's, comes by itself without the brothers paying for food.
